focus.label: Adjective: bonito
focus.summary: Bonito changes for both gender and number: bonito, bonita, bonitos, bonitas.

focus.label: Adjective: pequeño
focus.summary: Pequeño keeps the ñ and changes its ending for gender and number.

focus.label: Definite articles with surprising noun endings
focus.resultTitle: Gender belongs to the noun, not its final letter
focus.summary: Problema and mapa are masculine; mano and foto are feminine. Their articles and adjectives reveal the grammatical gender.

focus.label: Demonstrative: este
focus.summary: Este changes to esta, estos, or estas to match the noun that follows it.

focus.label: Adjective: trabajador
focus.summary: Adjectives ending in -dor add -a for feminine forms and mark the plural with -es or -as.

focus.label: Adjective: verde
focus.summary: Verde is the same for masculine and feminine nouns; only the plural changes it to verdes.

focus.label: Indefinite articles: un, una, unos, unas
focus.summary: Un, una, unos, and unas agree with grammatical gender and number, including masculine nouns such as día and idioma.

focus.label: Adjective: feliz
focus.summary: Feliz works with masculine and feminine singular nouns; its plural form is felices.

focus.label: Our: agreement with the possessed noun
focus.resultTitle: Our: agreement with the possessed noun
focus.summary: Nuestro agrees with the thing possessed, not with the gender of the people who own it.

focus.label: First: forms before a noun
focus.summary: Before a masculine singular noun, primero shortens to primer. The other forms here are primera, primeros and primeras.

focus.label: Better: number agreement
focus.summary: Mejor has the same form for masculine and feminine nouns. Use mejores with plural nouns.

focus.label: Definite articles: el, la, los, las
focus.summary: Use el or la with one noun, and los or las with plural nouns. The article agrees with the noun in gender and number.

focus.label: Adjective: grande
focus.summary: Grande does not change for gender. Use grandes with plural nouns. In these phrases it follows the noun and means big.

focus.label: Possessives: mi and mis
focus.summary: The short possessive mi becomes mis before plural nouns. It does not change for masculine and feminine nouns.
